steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: ...We were so close...

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: If you hadn't knocked me out, I would've made it. At least we would've been together...

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: ...I couldn't let you throw your life away.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: The military's in chaos. This is our opening. We move two days from now, gathering allies inside the city. But to unite them, we need a symbol. The guerrilla banner. And your name.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: When we win, DisCity goes independent. The metropoles won't take it lying down. First, they'll cut supplies. Then they'll invade. It'll probably be more nuclear strikes coming.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Then the real fight begins. Fear everywhere. The city's gonna need hope, and you're the one who gives it to them. Isn't that what you do best?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: So live. Do what only you can do.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Heh... You're right... You're damn right...

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: I can't die... Not now. She's waiting... waiting for me to bring her victory. I'll live—long enough to make every last one of them pay.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Catherine was right. Our gear's garbage. We need better. We must close the gap.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Let's move. The bunker at Nirvana Port is still stuffed with weapons we got last time. All the Andohar gear Helena bled to save. It's all there.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: We're going in, taking it all back... and then we're gonna break their legs with their own damn guns!
Battle Report—from Dravyn
That's what Brock told me. And I believe he meant every word of it. He was going to use the enemy's own guns to kill them all.

June 17th to June 29th. Brock led search and rescue in the ruins of Nirvana Port. July 3rd. Brock escorted the survivors and supplies back to camp. July 10th. Brock met with every unit of the guerrillas. Handed out commendation medals he'd made himself. July 25th. Brock led the assault that destroyed the remaining missile silos left behind by the metropoles. August 27th. Brock united the DisCity army and staged the mutiny.
He still died, after giving his speech, after seeing the Independence Army formally established.
[Speech]

September 15, N.F. 66
DisCity

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: I never thought I'd come back like this.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Five years ago, when Speaker Damon was assassinated by the metropoles, I left the military. I joined the guerrillas to avenge my friend. After the massacre at Nirvana Port, I left WhiteSands and returned to the army. Both journeys were soaked in this city's blood and suffering.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: All this time, DisCity has endured tragedy after tragedy. We've carried anger, fear, and grief. Some of us swore revenge. Others grew tired, wanting to compromise, to step back.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: But we all know the truth: concessions won't earn us respect. Our suffering was never caused by "disobedience." It comes from one thing: a lack of "independence."

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: We have no sovereignty. No means to defend ourselves. That's what gives them power to trample over us—whenever they want.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: And that's exactly why the Independence Army was born. That's why we keep growing stronger.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: We're not just guerrillas and DisCity soldiers. We are councilors, teachers, workers, scientists. People from every walk of life, standing together on the same front.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Stay clear. Stay rational. Stay brave. We will overcome grief and fear. Even if it takes one year, ten, or twenty, our goal will never change.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: DisCity will be independent. Sovereignty belongs unconditionally to the people. We must win this. And we will win.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: A cause that inspires generations to face death without flinching? That cause... is bound to triumph.
In all his years of giving speeches, that last one was his best. But he had a terrible first draft. He threw it away. I fished it out of the trash.

"From now on, more people will step onto this battlefield. They will witness death. They will experience loss. They will kill... To achieve victory, their souls will never be clean again. That is the true sacrifice. And we must honor it. If we cannot avoid this bloody path, then we cannot only bring back hatred and death."

"We must fight to eliminate injustice. To forge something new, for survival, justice, peace, love. We must trade those battles and sacrifices for a better future. This is the promise we have to make them believe. And then we have to fulfill it. That is the only way to truly honor their sacrifice."
"That way... even with blood on their hands... they can walk through hell with a clear conscience."
Speech concluded, he rendered a bold salute, then marched with commanding strides down the long steps and back behind the stage.
The moment he was out of the audience's sight, he collapsed.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: ...Brock!
And just like that... the leader of the guerrilla movement, the first commander of the Independence Army, was gone.

The cause was radiation poisoning. On a rescue op, his protective suit was damaged. But he didn't fall back. Pulled two of our people out of the hot zone. And while he was at it, he secured those rare pits we desperately needed.
He held on for three months after that. Fought like hell to live. Until now.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Gasp... Gasp... Well, I did my best, buddy... Just... couldn't finish the job... Don't go holding that against me, alright...

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Is Death coming for me... I can see my wife...

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Wait! Don't you dare... Catherine!! We need a medic over here, NOW!!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: You are not dying here. I'll do whatever it takes, just stay with us! Do you hear me?!!

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Ah... In that case... You're gonna have to... finish the job for me...

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: DisCity... It's... in your hands now...

The city gave Brock a simple funeral. A soldier's funeral. His final words lit a fire, just like he wanted. A new conviction in everyone who stands against the metropoles. On the ground, our fighters have a purpose. They're no longer lost.
But he still left me with the same question—
If conviction doesn't win the war, what's the value of the battle? What's the point of the sacrifice?
He gave them a flame, but he couldn't change the reality of this war. Even that Andohar brat knows it.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Right before the explosion, Brock sent every last transport vehicle he had. Helena shoved me onto one and told me to get out of Nirvana Port.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: She stayed. Said those captured weapons meant a lot to Brock... that she had to go and salvage them.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: ...As if any of that junk could last a second against a nuke.
And yet, she didn't run away from the guerrillas. I saw her at the funeral. Dressed in black, standing with the rest of us.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: That nuke was bought from the Andohar family. I know it better than anyone. So trust me, it wasn't the only one. A strike like that will happen again.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: As the new commander of the DisCity Independence Army, can you accept that?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: ...I can't.
